Assuming the B-tree is of order m, a B-tree node can store at most m-1 keys (5B each) and their corresponding record addresses (5B), m child pointers (5B each), and an integer indicating the actual number of keys in the node (2B), the following equation holds:
(2*(m-1)+m)*5 +2 ≤ 4000, which calculates to m ≤ 267. An index node can store at most m-1=266 index entries, and at least m/2|-1=133 index entries.
